Container.Name: Fightarr
Container.Overview:
UFC event manager for Usenet and Plex. Automatically searches, grabs, renames, and imports UFC fight cards — the Radarr for UFC that Radarr refuses to be.
IMPORTANT — PATH SETUP (read before installing):
For Fightarr to import completed downloads into your library, it MUST see the same paths as your download client (SABnzbd / NZBGet / qBittorrent) AND your media server (Plex / Jellyfin). The Servarr/TRaSH-Guides convention is a single /data mount that holds both downloads and media:
/mnt/user/data/usenet/complete/ ← SAB drops finished downloads here /mnt/user/data/media/ufc/ ← Fightarr renames + hardlinks here, Plex reads here
The default mount below maps your Unraid /mnt/user/data share into Fightarr as /data, matching the same convention you should use in SABnzbd, qBittorrent, and Plex/Jellyfin. This way hardlinks work (no double disk usage) and Fightarr can read whatever SAB writes.
After install, in Fightarr Settings → Media Management, set "Root Folder" to /data/media/ufc. In SABnzbd's category settings, set the "ufc" category folder to /data/usenet/complete/ufc.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Web UI and API port. Use 7879 to avoid conflict with Radarr (which also uses 7878). Access Fightarr at http://[IP]:[PORT:7879]/

Config.Name: Config
Config.Description: Stores the SQLite database, indexer/client credentials, and the in-memory log buffer. NEVER share this with another container — it contains API keys.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: REQUIRED. Unified data share holding both your downloads and your media library. Mount the SAME host path in your download client (SABnzbd/NZBGet/qBittorrent) and in Plex/Jellyfin so hardlinks work and Fightarr can find what SAB downloads. Inside this share use /data/usenet/complete/ for SAB and /data/media/ufc/ for the library. If you already have separate /downloads and /media shares, see the optional Downloads/Media mounts below.

Config.Name: Downloads (legacy / optional)
Config.Description: ONLY use this if your download client mounts /downloads separately instead of /data. The path here MUST match what SABnzbd sees as its complete-download folder. Leave blank if using the /data unified mount above.

Config.Name: Media (legacy / optional)
Config.Description: ONLY use this if your Plex/Jellyfin mounts /media separately instead of /data. Leave blank if using the /data unified mount above. If set, Fightarr's media root must be inside this path.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: Run-as user ID. 99 = nobody on Unraid. Must match the UID that owns /data so the importer can read SAB downloads and write to your media share.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Run-as group ID. 100 = users on Unraid. Must match the GID that owns /data.

Config.Name: UMASK
Config.Description: File permission mask for created files. 002 = group-writable, matches Radarr/Sonarr defaults so all your *arr containers produce compatible permissions.

Config.Name: TZ
Config.Description: Timezone (e.g. America/New_York, Europe/London). Affects scheduled-task timing and log timestamps.

Config.Name: Log Level
Config.Description: Logging verbosity: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR. Set to DEBUG only when troubleshooting — produces a lot of output.

Config.Name: TMDB API Key
Config.Description: Optional. Enables higher-quality TMDB poster art. Poster art works out of the box via Wikipedia without this key.

Config.Name: Plex Host
Config.Description: Optional. Plex server URL for library refresh after import, e.g. http://192.168.1.10:32400. Can also be configured in Fightarr Settings → Connect.

Config.Name: Plex Section ID
Config.Description: Optional. Plex library section ID to refresh. Leave blank to refresh all sections.

Config.Name: Jellyfin Host
Config.Description: Optional. Jellyfin server URL for library refresh after import, e.g. http://192.168.1.10:8096

Config.Name: CORS Origins
Config.Description: Comma-separated allowed origins for CORS, or * to allow all. Default * is fine for LAN-only deployments. Tighten this if you reverse-proxy Fightarr to the public internet.

Config.Name: Schedule Refresh Interval
Config.Description: How often (seconds) to sync the UFC schedule from Wikipedia. Default: 21600 (6 hours).

Config.Name: Indexer Search Interval
Config.Description: How often (seconds) to RSS-search indexers for monitored missing events. Default: 1800 (30 minutes). Same default as Radarr.
